clue.text: See how long archer takes we'll know eventually

parts.note: the question how long asks for a length of time
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer, shortened to Will Tell

explanation.surface: Wait and see how long the archer needs; all will be revealed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'takes' are link words: the time that Will Tell, the famous archer who shot an apple off his son's head, takes. The phrase then reads as a whole as the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb promises that the truth will come out once enough of the future has passed.

clue.text: Touching coloured man

parts.note: tan means coloured brown, as by the sun
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A moving remark about a man of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a line meeting a curve at a single point without crossing it is said to be touching it.

clue.text: Male relations are inside with all the chaps

indicators.note: the relations are placed inside the word for with

parts.note: and means with, joining things together
kin means family relations

explanation.surface: Men's family members sit indoors with all the other blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The human race, loosely put as every man and chap together.

clue.text: All in disorder, due to Shaw

indicators.note: disorder tells us the letters of the next words are put in a jumbled state

explanation.surface: Everything is a mess, and it is all the fault of the playwright Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All in' seems to be part of 'all in disorder', but it is the definition, meaning exhausted; 'disorder' alone signals the rearrangement of DUE TO SHAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all in is British slang for being completely exhausted, drained of colour and energy.

clue.text: Northerners fail to maintain standards in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to lapse is to slip from a standard one should keep

explanation.surface: People from the north are letting their standards slip in the way they talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami people of Lapland, in the far north of Scandinavia, were long called by this older name.

clue.text: For instance, divide up taxes

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
to allot is to divide up and share out

explanation.surface: To give one example, a government shares out taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks as if it belongs to 'divide up', but in this down clue it turns the whole run EG ALLOT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollage is a charge levied for passage or use, a form of duty.

clue.text: Young, out of form

parts.note: a form is the grassy hollow a hare rests in, so its young emerges from one; the surface suggests a youngster off form

explanation.surface: A youngster has lost their touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of form' looks like a sporting slump, but a hare's form is its nest, and the young hare comes out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year is called by this name, and hares shelter in hollows called forms.

clue.text: Feeble walk tired man out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A weak stroll wears a tired fellow out.
explanation.definitionFit: Watered-down milk is thin and insipid, hence a weak or wishy-washy idea or person.

clue.text: Spell "trespassing" with s in the wrong place

indicators.note: the letter named is shifted to a different spot in the word

parts.note: to trespass in the biblical sense is to sin, so trespassing means sinning
the letter s as printed

explanation.surface: A spelling lesson: the word trespassing has its s misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like an instruction to spell a word, but it is the definition, a period of play. Moving the first S of SINNING to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batting side's or player's turn at the crease is a spell at bat.

clue.text: Affair with a friend, say

parts.note: pal is a friend
to aver is to say firmly

explanation.surface: An affair with a friend, shall we say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests a romance, but it means a fuss or business.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, fussy business or rigmarole can be called an affair, as in what an affair that was.

clue.text: It's a memorable occasion when the final demand comes

definitions.text: It's a memorable occasion when the final demand comes

parts.words: It's a memorable occasion when the final demand comes
parts.note: a final demand for payment is traditionally printed in red ink, so the day such a letter lands is red-lettered

explanation.surface: A big day arrives along with the last reminder of an unpaid bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Feast days were marked in red on old calendars, so a special day is red-lettered.

clue.text: Viceroy — he had (and I have) to follow the king

indicators.note: the contracted pieces come after the king in the answer

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
he had contracts to he'd
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A viceroy, he and I both, had to walk behind the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes in HE'D and I'VE are dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Khedive ruled Egypt as the Ottoman sultan's governor, a viceroy's role.

clue.text: Took the lead and looked right in

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation is placed inside the word for looked

parts.note: stared means looked intently

explanation.surface: Someone went first and glanced to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right in' looks like 'right in' as one phrase, but 'in' puts R inside STARED.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who plays the lead role in a film is said to have been its star.

clue.text: Saw that's famous

explanation.definitionFit: Saw means observed or remarked upon; famous means well known and celebrated.

clue.text: Force often not starting to move away from the middle

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters are shifted about into a new order
the word often loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Force often fails to get anything going when pushing away from the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the O of 'often' to leave FTEN; 'to move' rearranges FORCE plus FTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed not at the exact centre point is offset to one side.

clue.text: Headed towards an opening, play with Helen and Edward

parts.note: fun means play or amusement
Nell is a familiar form of Helen
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Making for a gap, having a game with Helen and Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Things channelled through a narrowing cone are steered towards the narrow mouth.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, like Mary Jane's suitor

annotationWithheld.why: Old-fashioned, like Mary Jane's suitor (4-5): 'Old-fashioned' defines WORM-EATEN, but the allusion in 'like Mary Jane's suitor' could not be identified, so the second half cannot be explained honestly

clue.text: Refuse to smooth over a mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to rub is to smooth by friction
bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: Declining to gloss over an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, waste. BISH is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish and refuse are both words for household waste thrown away.

clue.text: Meritocracy — it's introduced into plant

indicators.note: the expanded words are put inside the plant

parts.note: the elm is a tree, a plant
it's expands to it is

explanation.surface: Rule by the able is planted into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: IT'S must be expanded to IT IS before going inside ELM.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism favours a select, supposedly superior few, as a meritocracy rewards the most able.

clue.text: Understood I'd be employed in diplomacy

indicators.note: the letter is used inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact means diplomacy and sensitivity
read as I would, giving the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they would make a good diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'd be employed in' as 'I would be employed in': the I goes inside TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is unspoken but implied, understood without words.

clue.text: Sumatra producing, several shocks

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: The island of Sumatra gives rise to a series of earthquakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumas are severe emotional or physical jolts.

clue.text: Spanish boat with British name

parts.note: cat is short for catboat or catamaran
Alan is a common British first name

explanation.surface: A Spanish vessel bearing a British name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish' is the definition: Catalan is a language and people of north-east Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia lies in Spain, so its people and language are Spanish in the broad sense.

clue.text: Proposing to discuss Bill with Heather

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Suggesting a talk about Bill and Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Heather' pose as people. In Britain, tabling a motion means putting it forward for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to put a matter on the table is to submit it for debate.

clue.text: Stakes for fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Gages are pledges deposited as security; gages are also greengage plums.

clue.text: One claiming payment from former player

parts.note: ex means former
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A retired performer asks to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor demands money due, such as a tax gatherer.

clue.text: Being a king, we hear, and governing

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: a king on the throne is reigning

explanation.surface: A monarch rules, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Reining in a horse means controlling it, hence directing and keeping in check.

clue.text: Plate hit girl

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl was struck by a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin layer, scale or plate, as in a gill.

clue.text: Inventor had to miss one development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An inventor had to skip one stage of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: The American who patented the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.
